title: Shoreline Labs POC infosec evidence & action plan
content:
Executive summary:

This document is the working evidence packet and open action plan for the Shoreline Labs POC (Retail analytics, regulated PII flows). Goal: provide Shoreline with answers to their security questionnaire, sample artifacts (config snippets, logs, certs), and a prioritized remediation/action list for any gaps. This is an internal working draft — many attachments are draft exports from our test environment.

Scope and constraints:
- Product surface: Redwood Hosted API for embeddings and chat + Dedicated VPC option for sensitive workloads.
- Customer asks: encryption at rest + in transit, bring-your-own-key (BYOK) integration, VPC peering or PrivateLink, audit logs for 365 days, SOC2-type control mapping.
- Out of scope: full SOC2 report delivery (we will provide current SOC2 attestations and control mappings only).

Questionnaire summary (high level responses):
- Data classification: We treat model inputs as customer data. Shoreline PII processed under customer tenancy/isolated Dedicated config when required.
- Encryption in transit: TLS 1.3 enforced on all public endpoints. Mutual TLS available for Dedicated endpoints on request.
- Encryption at rest: All persisted data (kv cache for private deployments, model runtime artifacts) encrypted with AES-256. Keys are managed by either Redwood KMS or customer KMS (BYOK) in Private deployments.
- Key management: Redwood integrates with AWS KMS and GCP KMS for Hosted and Dedicated; for Private deployments we support KMIP-compatible HSM or cloud KMS via customer-managed credentials.
- Access control & auth: RBAC via Console + API key tokens. SSO via OIDC/SAML for console access. API requests can be scoped to tokens with route/model restrictions.
- Auditability: Request and token-level logs available; admin actions (deploy, grant-role) logged. Default retention: 90 days for hosted logs, configurable to 365 days as an enterprise add-on.

Evidence index (attached/delivered artifacts):
1) network-architecture-shoreline-dedicated.pdf — diagram showing VPC peering, NAT, subnets, security groups.
2) tls-cert-chain-sample.txt — public cert chain for the POC endpoint (sanitized).
3) kms-config-snippet.yaml — example showing integration with customer KMS (placeholder ARNs).
4) audit-sample-2025-11.jsonl — redacted audit log export for 7-day window from test workload.
5) soc2-snapshot-2025.pdf — current SOC2 coverage summary (redacted).
6) pen-test-summary-2024.pdf — executive summary of most recent 3rd-party pentest and remediation status.
7) hsm-compatibility-matrix.csv — supported HSM models and required firmware/KMIP levels.

Evidence mapping (question -> artifact):
- Q: How do you manage keys? -> A: kms-config-snippet.yaml, hsm-compatibility-matrix.csv, soc2-snapshot-2025.pdf
- Q: Can we retain logs 1 year? -> A: audit-sample-2025-11.jsonl + linked_artifacts: jira:SEC-4123 (retention enhancement ticket)
- Q: Network separation? -> A: network-architecture-shoreline-dedicated.pdf

Detailed technical notes (working):
- TLS: Enforce TLS 1.3 ciphers; we will provide HSTS + ALPN. For Dedicated we can enable mTLS; steps to onboard Shoreline CA into our trust store are noted in kms-config-snippet.yaml.
- KMS/BYOK: For POC we used a test key in the customer's AWS account (arn:aws:kms:...:sample) — replaced with placeholders in artifacts. For Private deployments, recommend using customer-managed KMS with CMKs and automatic rotation per Shoreline policy.
- Data residency: POC was run in us-west-2 region. Customer required EU residency for production; we proposed deploying Dedicated in eu-west-1 or Private on-prem. See architecture PDF for region mapping.
- Logging: Token-level hashing applied to avoid storing raw API keys. Request payloads retained in logs only for debugging with customer approval.

Open items and action plan (owner — due):
- A1: Confirm Shoreline desired log retention SLA (90/180/365) and enable 365-day export pipeline if needed — Owner: Priya Rangan — Due: 2026-01-27
- A2: Formalize BYOK onboarding playbook and checklist (steps for granting KMS permissions, IAM roles, rotation policy) — Owner: Jonas Meyer — Due: 2025-11-17
- A3: Produce mTLS onboarding sample and cert signing request template for Shoreline CA — Owner: Ethan Cole — Due: 2025-11-10 (in progress)
- A4: Validate HSM vendor firmware compatibility with customer HSM (Thales Luna test planned) — Owner: Maya Chen — Due: 2026-02-05
- A5: Update audit log redaction policy to exclude raw PII by default; produce sample redaction transform — Owner: Aisha Patel — Due: 2026-01-15

Residual risks (for customer readout):
- Risk: Hosted model telemetry may surface derived PII in debug traces if full payload logging is enabled. Mitigation: default logging redaction + option to run Dedicated/Private where debug traces are disabled.
- Risk: Customer-managed KMS onboarding increases operational complexity and may delay rollouts. Mitigation: provide template IAM policy and temporary escrow key for initial testing.

Meeting notes (2025-11-04 kick-off with Shoreline security):
- Shoreline asked for explicit support for HSM-backed keys and a sample contract clause for key custody.
- They requested a 365-day log retention for audit purposes, with weekly exports to their S3. We recommended a staged approach: 90-day hosted retention + 365-day push for Dedicated.
- Action: Solutions-eng to produce required artifacts and evidence by next sync (2025-11-17).

Attachments in Drive (current exports):
- network-architecture-shoreline-dedicated.pdf
- tls-cert-chain-sample.txt
- kms-config-snippet.yaml
- audit-sample-2025-11.jsonl
- soc2-snapshot-2025.pdf
- pen-test-summary-2024.pdf
- hsm-compatibility-matrix.csv

How to validate this packet (internal checklist):
- Confirm all sample ARNs/keys are redacted. (YES: kms-config-snippet.yaml)
- Ensure no customer PII in audit sample. (IN PROGRESS: audit-sample-2025-11.jsonl redaction notes included)
- Verify attached SOC2 snapshot is the latest vendor-signed PDF. (DONE)
- Cross-reference Jira SEC-4123 for retention pipeline status. (OPEN)

Notes to self / rough ideas: 
- Consider adding a short-runbook for emergency key rotation in Dedicated mode (one-page checklist).
- Draft contractual wording for "no model training on customer inputs" if Shoreline requires that guarantee (we currently guarantee non-training in Dedicated/Private; hosted API depends on contract).

Next steps prior to customer deliverable:
- Clean up artifacts, embed non-sensitive diagrams into a single zip, and route to legal for one-off contract clause review.
- Run final redaction pass on audit samples.
- Hold internal review with Security (Maya + Security Ops) on BYOK playbook.

Slack/threads and references: 
- See thread #shoreline-poc-2025 for async Q&A and sample keys (redacted).
- Linked Jira: SEC-4123 (retention), SEC-4178 (BYOK playbook), ENG-2244 (mTLS support).

Appendix: sample KMS onboarding checklist (short):
1) Customer creates CMK in their KMS and grants Redwood's service principal Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey permissions.
2) Customer provides KMS key ARN and cross-account trust docs.
3) Redwood validates the key by performing a test GenerateDataKey call in a staging account.
4) Once validated, Redwood configures runtime to reference the CMK ARN and documents rotation schedule in the runbook.

End of packet (working).

If you are reviewing: please add comments inline in Drive or ping me in Slack. This file will be converted to a customer-facing PDF after sign-off from Security and Legal.
